purpose: AI reading and task-routing index; not an authorization or ready-to-deploy configuration

version_compatibility.1.10.0: Installed on the reference RTX 3060 VM. H264/HEVC hardware encoder creation unavailable (-12908); software encode to NVIDIA hardware decode passed pixel tests. Companion GlideBeam software-h264-fallback code uses Apple software H264 with Windows GPU decode. The existing released GlideBeam 0.2.0 download has no fallback; verify actual build source before upgrading.

constraints: Preserve existing VM identity; initialize only a new VM.
Never publish filled EFI, XML, OSK, credentials, images or unredacted logs.
Resize only an idle VFIO-owned matching GPU pair with supported BAR and enough MMIO.
Do not invoke libvirt from its QEMU hook.
Verify guest VNC/SSH before removing the virtual display.
Keep QEMU AppleSMC and use -vsmccomp; expect one AppleSMC service.
Keep ProvideCustomSlide=true and host-managed GPU BAR settings at -1.
API success is not pixel correctness or full application qualification.
known_limits: HEVC hardware encode failed pixel correctness on 1.1.0/1.9.0; hardware encoder creation is unavailable on RTX 3060 with 1.10.0.
The software path increases CPU usage; 1080p/30 FPS and 8 Mbps are configuration targets, not measured guarantees.
The existing GlideBeam 0.2.0 release lacks fallback; the companion source change and deployed validation build are separate from that release.
H264 bitrate control on prior NVIDIA hardware paths was not qualified; fixed QP behavior was observed on 1.1.0.
ES CPU marketing name remains Unknown; some CPUID fields round to 16/32.
Small OpenCL probes passed; no full Geekbench, GPU workload, long-run stability, other GPU or Apple ID qualification.
Generic exported scripts were not replayed end-to-end on another host.
